㊢ (what I did) I loaded the current `session-turn-analysis.el` into your Emacs. The recorder is still `files`, so nothing changes until you switch it. 象 is on, with policy `all`.

㊭ (watching the JVM test) For the turn after you switch, there are three things to check:
1. It shows up in evidence under the `xiang-turn` tag: `curl -s 'localhost:7070/api/alpha/evidence?tag=xiang-turn&limit=5'`. There are none so far, which is expected, since nothing has gone through the JVM yet.
2. When my reply ends, `/api/alpha/xiang/health` shows it outstanding.
3. When the reading lands, the stepper refreshes on its own and a second evidence entry appears, the reading, linked to the turn record.

If any of these doesn't happen, tell me which and I'll trace it. `(setq session-mode-turn-recorder 'files)` switches back.

previous_reply_acts.text: (Tickle) Work orders do give Tickle a new role. As built, Tickle pages an agent after 300 seconds without new evidence and then escalates to a restart. I suspect that's why it was such a pain: silence is the wrong signal. With work orders, Tickle could act only when an order is open, the agent that owes it has no running job and isn't parked, and no reminder has been sent. I've added this to `E-agency-work-orders.md` (committed `d7f45ee8`, pushed).

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(why silence fails) `detect-stalls` in `src/futon3c/agents/tickle.clj` treats "no evidence for `:threshold-seconds`" (default 300) as stalled. It gets both cases wrong:
- An idle agent that owes nothing gets paged.
- An agent busy on something else while it owes an order looks alive.
